definition_en: an action or event that causes public shock and disapproval
core_image: 报纸头版印着醒目的标题，路人停下脚步议论纷纷
scene: 报纸头版爆出公司财务丑闻。 The newspaper revealed a financial scandal.
sceneCN: 这里 scandal 是「丑闻」（第 1 个义项）；句意：报纸揭露了一起财务丑闻。

senses.title: Public disgrace
senses.definition: an action or event that causes public shock and disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 引起公众震惊与谴责的行为或事件
senses.example: The minister resigned over a corruption scandal.
senses.exampleCN: 部长因腐败丑闻辞职。
senses.why: The core sense is a public shock that damages reputation.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是损害名誉的公共震惊事件。

senses.title: Malicious gossip
senses.definition: talk that spreads shocking or unkind stories about people
senses.definitionCN: 传播关于他人的惊人或不友善故事的闲话
senses.example: The village was full of scandal about the new neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 村里到处都是关于新邻居的流言。
senses.why: The shock of an event feeds the talk that spreads it.
senses.whyCN: 事件的震惊滋养了传播它的闲话。

senses.title: Moral outrage
senses.definition: a feeling of shock and moral disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 震惊与道德上的不赞同之感
senses.example: Their behaviour caused scandal among the older guests.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的行为在年长宾客中引起反感。
senses.why: The event produces the emotion it is named for.
senses.whyCN: 事件产生了以之命名的情绪。

intro.en: Scandal comes from Greek skandalon, a trap or stumbling block, through Latin.
intro.cn: scandal 经拉丁语源自希腊语 skandalon，意为陷阱或绊脚石。

items.en: Skandalon means a snare or a cause of stumbling.
items.cn: skandalon 意为圈套或使人跌倒的原因。

items.en: Scandalum meant a stumbling block or offence.
items.cn: scandalum 意为绊脚石或冒犯。

items.en: Scandale carried the sense of public disgrace.
items.cn: scandale 带有公开耻辱之义。

items.en: Scandal named shameful conduct and gossip.
items.cn: scandal 指可耻行为与流言。

items.en: Scandal covers politics, business, and celebrity life.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scandal 涵盖政治、商业与名人生活。

note.en: Scandal is compared with similar spellings and with words for shame and gossip.
note.cn: 把 scandal 与形近词以及表示耻辱和流言的词作比较。

entries.definition: a strong feeling of shock and anger
talk about other people's private lives

normalIntro.en: Scandal can be remembered through its sense of a public stumble.
normalIntro.cn: 可以通过「当众跌倒」的意思记住 scandal。

normal.en: A scandal is a public stumble that everyone sees.
normal.cn: 丑闻是所有人都看见的当众失足。

normal.en: The word has scan at the beginning and dal at the end.
normal.cn: 这个词开头是 scan，结尾是 dal。

normal.en: A corruption scandal often ends a career.
normal.cn: 腐败丑闻常常终结一个人的职业生涯。

normal.en: Scandalous describes behaviour that shocks people.
normal.cn: scandalous 形容令人震惊的行为。

normal.en: A scandal sheet is a paper full of gossip.
normal.cn: scandal sheet 是充满八卦的小报。

abstract.en: A scandal is a private failure made public.
abstract.cn: 丑闻是被公开的私人失败。

abstract.en: Gossip spreads a scandal faster than facts can.
abstract.cn: 流言传播丑闻比事实更快。

abstract.en: The word once meant a trap, and a scandal still catches people.
abstract.cn: 这个词原指陷阱，而丑闻至今仍会让人中招。

examples.en: The scandal damaged the company's reputation.
examples.cn: 这起丑闻损害了公司的声誉。

examples.en: Reporters kept the scandal alive for weeks.
examples.cn: 记者们让这桩丑闻持续发酵了数周。

examples.en: She refused to take part in the gossip and scandal.
examples.cn: 她拒绝参与那些流言蜚语。

dict_mnemonic.text: scandal 原指「绊倒人的陷阱」，一个人当众跌倒就成丑闻；可记「当众失足，满城风雨」。

root: 源自希腊语 skandalon（陷阱、绊脚石），经拉丁语 scandalum 入英语，核心义「使人跌倒、招致公愤的事」。

sensesIntro.en: Scandal means a shocking public event, the gossip around it, or the outrage it causes.
sensesIntro.cn: scandal 意为令人震惊的公开事件、围绕它的流言，或它引起的愤慨。

core.en: A public shock caused by shameful behaviour.
core.cn: 可耻行为引起的公众震惊。

branches.en: The core event that shocks the public.
branches.cn: 震惊公众的核心事件。

branches.en: Talk that spreads the shocking story.
branches.cn: 传播惊人故事的闲话。

branches.en: The moral outrage felt by observers.
branches.cn: 旁观者感到的道德愤慨。

branches.en: An event and the gossip about it feed each other.
branches.cn: 事件与关于它的流言相互助长。

branches.en: A shameful event produces public outrage.
branches.cn: 可耻事件引发公众愤慨。

intro.en: Scandal has a family of adjectives, verbs, and compounds.
intro.cn: scandal 有形容词、动词和复合词构成的词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin scandalum, a stumbling block, is the direct source.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 scandalum（绊脚石）是直接来源。

items.exampleCN: 这番话让观众大为震惊。
散布丑闻的人毁了她的名声。

items.example: He never reads a scandal sheet.

items.exampleCN: 受丑闻打击的银行失去了客户。

definition_en: a word that joins other words or clauses, or the act of joining two things
core_image: 两段铁轨在同一处接头，被一块夹板牢牢锁住
scene: 老师让学生把两个短句合成一句。 Write two clauses, then join them with a conjunction.
sceneCN: 这里 conjunction 指「连词」（第 1 个义项：连接词或分句的虚词）；句意是先写两个分句，再用一个连词把它们连起来。

senses.title: The joining word
senses.definition: a word such as and or but that joins words or clauses
senses.definitionCN: 像 and 或 but 这样连接词或分句的虚词
senses.example: Put a conjunction between the two clauses.
senses.exampleCN: 在两个分句之间放一个连词。
senses.why: Two thoughts need a small bridge, and this word is that bridge.
senses.whyCN: 两个念头之间需要一座小桥，而这个词就是那座桥。

senses.title: A joining together
senses.definition: the state of two or more things being joined or working together
senses.definitionCN: 两件或多件事物结合、共同作用的状态
senses.example: The show is a conjunction of art and science.
senses.exampleCN: 这场展览是艺术与科学的结合。
senses.why: Things that meet at one point share a moment and a meaning.
senses.whyCN: 在同一点相遇的事物，共享一个时刻与一层意义。

senses.title: A rare alignment
senses.definition: an occasion when several events or planets meet at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 若干事件或天体同时相遇的时机
senses.example: Astrologers watched the conjunction of two planets.
senses.exampleCN: 占星者观察着两颗行星的会合。
senses.why: When separate paths cross at one point, people remember the crossing.
senses.whyCN: 当几条分开的路径交于一点，人们会记住这次交会。

intro.en: Conjunction comes from Latin coniunctio, a joining, from com-, together, and iungere, to join or yoke.
intro.cn: conjunction 来自拉丁语 coniunctio，意为连接，由 com-（一起）与 iungere（连接、套上轭）构成。

items.en: Iungere meant to join or yoke animals to one bar.
items.cn: iungere 意为把牲口套在同一根横木上。

items.en: Coniunctio named a joining of things or of words.
items.cn: coniunctio 指事物的连接，也指词语的连接。

items.en: Old French conjonction kept the grammar sense alive.
items.cn: 古法语 conjonction 把这个语法含义保留下来。

items.en: English conjunction entered as the name of a joining word.
items.cn: 英语 conjunction 最初就是连接词的名字。

items.en: It now also means any coming together of events.
items.cn: 如今它也指事件的任何一次同时发生。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin join base junct-, and the meaning group names other devices that hold parts together.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语连接词基 junct-，近义组列出其他把部分连在一起的东西。

entries.definition: a place where roads or railway lines meet
an official order to do or stop something
a thing that joins two parts
the joining of separate groups into one

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a hinge between two clauses, then move to two events meeting and to a railway joint.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从两个分句之间的铰链开始，再到两件事的相遇与铁轨的接头。

normal.en: Con- is together and junct- is join, so a conjunction joins two parts.
normal.cn: con- 是一起，junct- 是连接，所以连词就是把两部分接起来。

normal.en: And, but, because: three small bridges in one sentence.
normal.cn: and、but、because：一句话里的三座小桥。

normal.en: A conjunction is a hinge on which two doors of meaning swing.
normal.cn: 连词是一副铰链，两扇意义的门靠它开合。

normal.en: When two events happen at once, people call that a conjunction too.
normal.cn: 当两件事同时发生，人们也把这称作一次会合。

normal.en: Remove the word and the sentence falls into two pieces, so it was a conjunction.
normal.cn: 把这个词拿走，句子就散成两半，说明它就是连词。

abstract.en: Picture two rails locked by one steel plate.
abstract.cn: 想象两段钢轨被一块钢板锁在一起。

abstract.en: Picture a hinge that lets two doors move as one.
abstract.cn: 想象一副让两扇门合为一体的铰链。

abstract.en: Picture two paths meeting under a single lamp.
abstract.cn: 想象两条小路在一盏灯下汇合。

examples.en: Use a conjunction to link the two ideas.
examples.cn: 用一个连词把这两个想法连起来。

examples.en: The festival is held in conjunction with the city library.
examples.cn: 这个节庆活动是与市图书馆联合举办的。

examples.en: A strange conjunction of weather and luck saved the harvest.
examples.cn: 天气与运气的奇妙巧合保住了这一季的收成。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 conjunction 记成 con（一起）加 junct（连接）：把两句话一起接起来的小词，就是连词。

root: 源自拉丁语 coniunctio（com 一起 + iungere 连接），本义是连接，后专指连接词，也指事件的会合。

sensesIntro.en: From a small grammar word, to any joining of two things, and finally to events meeting at one moment.
sensesIntro.cn: 从一个语法小词，到任何两物的结合，最后到事件在同一刻相遇。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hinge that holds two separate parts in one line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一副铰链把两个分开的部分连成一条线。

branches.en: The grammar sense is a single word doing the work of a hinge.
branches.cn: 语法义项就是一个词在承担铰链的工作。

branches.en: Two things joined can also work as one unit.
branches.cn: 被连接的两件事也能作为一个整体运作。

branches.en: Planets or events that meet in time form a rare conjunction.
branches.cn: 在时间上相遇的天体或事件构成罕见的会合。

branches.en: Both senses come from one image of parts held at a joint.
branches.cn: 两个义项都来自同一幅画面：部分被固定在一个接头上。

branches.en: A conjunction in the sky is only a joining seen from far away.
branches.cn: 天上的会合，不过是远看时的一次连接。

intro.en: Conjunction is built on Latin com-, together, plus iungere, to join.
intro.cn: conjunction 由拉丁语 com-（一起）与 iungere（连接）构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin join base junct- also appears in junction, injunction and disjointed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的连接词基 junct- 也出现在 junction、injunction 与 disjointed 中。

items.meaning: a joining word or a joining
items.example: A conjunction can join two clauses.
items.exampleCN: 连词可以连接两个分句。

items.example: The conjunctive tissue holds the parts.
items.exampleCN: 连接组织把这些部分固定住。
这两个问题是连在一起的。

items.meaning: an order that binds someone to act
items.exampleCN: 法院发出了一道强制令。
我们睡在相邻的房间里。

items.meaning: not connected in a clear order
items.example: His story was disjointed and vague.
items.exampleCN: 他的叙述支离破碎又含糊。

definition_en: the act of getting involved in something unasked, or unwanted disturbance of a signal or process
core_image: 收音机里音乐忽然被沙沙的杂音盖住，旋钮怎么也调不掉
scene: 老人反复拧着旧收音机的旋钮，沙沙声一阵一阵压住播音员的声音。 The referee stopped the game for interference with the goalkeeper.
sceneCN: 这里 interference 是「干扰、妨碍」（第 1 个义项：对信号或过程的扰乱），句意裁判因对守门员的干扰而中止比赛。画面里的物件：旧收音机、旋钮、裁判的手势。

derivatives.zh: 由本词去掉 -ence 构成，义为「干涉；干扰」
由动词分词构成，义为「爱插手的」
由否定前缀 non- 加本词构成，义为「不干涉」
由本词词干加 -on 构成，义为一种「干扰素」

senses.title: Meddling
senses.definition: the act of taking part in someone else's affairs without being asked
senses.definitionCN: 未经请求就参与别人的事务
senses.example: The deal failed because of constant interference from relatives.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔生意因亲戚们不断干涉而没成。
senses.why: It is the noun of action of interferire, to strike between.
senses.whyCN: 它是 interferire「在中间击打」这一动词的行为名词。

senses.title: Disturbance of a signal
senses.definition: unwanted noise or change in a signal caused by another source
senses.definitionCN: 由另一来源造成的信号中不受欢迎的噪声或变化
senses.example: The storm caused interference on every channel.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨使每个频道都出现干扰。
senses.why: Waves do strike across each other, and the engineers borrowed the old word.
senses.whyCN: 波真的会互相横穿，工程师便借用了这个古老的词。

senses.title: In sport and law
senses.definition: illegal obstruction of another player, or unlawful hindrance of a right
senses.definitionCN: 对另一名参赛者的违规阻挡，或对权利的非法妨碍
senses.example: Interference with witnesses is a serious offence.
senses.exampleCN: 妨碍证人是一项严重罪名。
senses.why: Rules need a name for a body or a right that gets struck across.
senses.whyCN: 规则需要一个词来指被横撞的身体或权利。

intro.en: Interference is the English noun formed on interfere, from Latin ferire "to strike".
intro.cn: interference 是在 interfere 之上构成的英语名词，源头是拉丁语 ferire「击打」。

items.en: Interferire meant to strike in between, a rare compound of ferire.
items.cn: interferire 意为「在中间击打」，是 ferire 的罕见合成。

items.en: S'entreférir described blows or hooves clashing against each other.
items.cn: s'entreférir 形容打击或马蹄互相撞击。

items.en: Eighteenth-century English formed interference from the verb.
items.cn: 十八世纪英语由这个动词构成 interference。

items.en: Nineteenth-century physics applied it to light waves that cross and cancel.
items.cn: 十九世纪物理学用它指相互交叉并相消的光波。

items.en: Radio and sport each gave it a fixed technical sense.
items.cn: 无线电与体育各自给它一个固定的专门含义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the striking root; the near-meaning group holds other words for disturbance.
note.cn: 形近组共享「击打」词根；近义组收其他表示扰乱的词。

entries.definition: The verb of meddling or disturbing.

entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「推论」，由证据得出的结论。

entries.definition: The way things are not the same.
An interruption of peace or order.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「骚动；打扰」，平静秩序被打断。
名词，义为「噪声」，单纯的不需要的声音。

entries.definition: Deliberate stepping in, often to help.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「介入」，常带有帮助之意。

normalIntro.en: The hooks tie the static on the radio to the old blow hidden in ferire.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把收音机里的沙沙声与 ferire 里那一记古老的击打连起来。

normal.en: Interference is a blow struck between two things that were working.
normal.cn: 干扰是打在两件本来好好的东西之间的一记。

normal.en: Electrical interference turns music into sand.
normal.cn: 电气干扰把音乐变成沙子。

normal.en: Government interference is welcome to some, resented by others.
normal.cn: 政府干预有人欢迎，也有人不满。

normal.en: Referees punish interference in the penalty area.
normal.cn: 裁判处罚禁区内的妨碍行为。

normal.en: Interference with evidence is a crime.
normal.cn: 妨碍证据是一项罪行。

abstract.en: Every signal has an enemy broadcasting on its channel.
abstract.cn: 每个信号都有个在它频道上广播的敌人。

abstract.en: Interference is contact you did not ask for.
abstract.cn: 干扰是未经请求的接触。

abstract.en: A quiet mind filters interference without fuss.
abstract.cn: 安静的心会不动声色地滤掉干扰。

examples.en: We finished the work without interference from anyone.
examples.cn: 我们完成这项工作，未受任何人干涉。

examples.en: Thick walls block much of the phone interference.
examples.cn: 厚墙挡住了大部分手机干扰。

examples.en: The club was fined for interference with the referee.
examples.cn: 俱乐部因妨碍裁判而被罚款。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因特费尔润斯」——网络特费劲，全是干扰

root: 拉丁语 ferire「击打」→ interferire「在中间打」→ 英语动词 interfere + -ence → interference。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: meddling, disturbance of signals, and hindrance in sport or law.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：插手他人事务、信号受扰，以及比赛或法律中的妨碍。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: music swallowed by static that the dial cannot remove.
core.cn: 核心意象：音乐被旋钮扭不掉的沙沙声吞没。

branches.en: THE RELATIVES: unwanted voices decide a private deal.
branches.cn: 亲戚这条线：不相干的声音决定私事。

branches.en: THE RADIO: another source overwrites the signal.
branches.cn: 收音机这条线：另一个来源覆盖了信号。

branches.en: THE PITCH: a body or a right is illegally obstructed.
branches.cn: 球场这条线：身体或权利被违规阻挡。

branches.en: THE LINK: meddling becomes punishable when a rule forbids it.
branches.cn: 连接线：一旦有规则禁止，插手便成为可罚之事。

branches.en: THE LINK: both are unwanted action arriving from outside.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都是从外面来的不受欢迎的动作。

intro.en: Interference = inter- "between" + fer- "strike" + -ence "state of".
intro.cn: interference = inter-「在……之间」+ fer-「击打」+ -ence「……的状态」。

latinIntro.en: Latin ferire and interferire are attested; the noun itself is English-made.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ferire 与 interferire 有记载，这个名词本身是英语构成。

items.example: It places the interference in the middle.
It forms non-interference, a policy word.

items.exampleCN: 它在生物学中构成 interferon。

items.example: The verb is the direct base.

definition_en: to bring people together, or to fit parts together into a whole
core_image: 散落的零件一件件拼合成整体
scene: 操场上哨声一响，各班开始排队。 The students assembled in the hall before noon.
sceneCN: 这里 assemble 是「集合」（第 1 个义项：人们聚到一处）；句意是学生们中午前在礼堂集合。

senses.title: To come together in a group
senses.definition: to gather people or to gather oneself in one place
senses.definitionCN: 把人聚到一处，或自身聚到一处
senses.example: The students assembled in the hall before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 学生们中午前在礼堂集合。
senses.why: Old French assembler came from Latin ad simul, 'to the same place', so the word begins as a gathering.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 assembler 来自拉丁语 ad simul「到同一处」，所以这个词本义就是聚集。

senses.title: To fit parts into a whole
senses.definition: to put separate pieces together so they work as one
senses.definitionCN: 把分开的部件拼在一起，使其作为一个整体运作
senses.example: Workers assemble the engines by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 工人们手工组装发动机。
senses.why: If parts are gathered in the right order, the gathering becomes construction; the same verb serves both.
senses.whyCN: 若把零件按正确次序聚到一起，聚集就成了装配；同一个动词兼指两者。

intro.en: Assemble goes back to a Latin phrase meaning 'to the same place'.
intro.cn: assemble 可追溯到意为「到同一处」的拉丁短语。

items.en: simul meant 'together, at the same time'.
items.cn: simul 意为「一起、同时」。

items.en: ad simul meant 'to the same place'.
items.cn: ad simul 意为「到同一处」。

items.en: assembler meant 'to gather together'.
items.cn: assembler 意为「聚拢」。

items.en: English assemble first meant to gather people.
items.cn: 英语 assemble 最初指聚集人群。

items.en: Industry gave it the sense of fitting parts.
items.cn: 工业赋予了它「拼装部件」义。

note.en: The look-alike group is the assembly family; the near-meaning group splits gathering from building.
note.cn: 形近组是 assembly 词族；近义组把聚集与建造分开。

entries.definition: a gathering or a putting together

normalIntro.en: Assemble gathers either people or parts.
normalIntro.cn: assemble 聚拢的要么是人，要么是零件。

normal.en: On a factory line, parts are assembled.
normal.cn: 流水线上组装的是零件。

normal.en: At school, students assemble for a meeting.
normal.cn: 学校里学生集合开会。

normal.en: The noun is assembly.
normal.cn: 名词是 assembly。

normal.en: The stress falls on the second syllable.
normal.cn: 重音落在第二个音节。

normal.en: The word has a silent final e before -ed.
normal.cn: 加 -ed 时词尾的 e 被省去。

abstract.en: See bolts being turned into a frame.
abstract.cn: 想象螺栓被拧进框架。

abstract.en: See rows of students filling a hall.
abstract.cn: 想象学生成排填满礼堂。

abstract.en: See a box of parts emptied on a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一盒零件倒在桌上。

examples.en: The students assembled in the hall before noon.
examples.cn: 学生们中午前在礼堂集合。

examples.en: Workers assemble the engines by hand.
examples.cn: 工人们手工组装发动机。

examples.en: The desk came fully assembled.
examples.cn: 这张桌子送来时已组装完毕。

dict_mnemonic.text: as-（向）加 sembl（一起）：往一处凑，人凑齐是集合，零件凑齐是组装。

root: 源自古法语 assembler「聚拢」，上溯拉丁语 ad simul「到同一处」；由人群聚集引申为部件装配。

sensesIntro.en: Gathering is the root, and parts gathered in order become a machine.
sensesIntro.cn: 聚集是词根；零件按序聚齐，就成了机器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: separate pieces drawn into one shape.
core.cn: 核心意象：分开的部件被收进同一个形状。

branches.en: assemble the staff
branches.cn: 召集员工

branches.en: assemble in the square
branches.cn: 在广场集合

branches.en: assemble a bike
branches.cn: 组装自行车

branches.en: assemble the parts
branches.cn: 装配零件

branches.en: easy to assemble
branches.cn: 易于组装

intro.en: A French verb of gathering that industry made technical.
intro.cn: 这是一个法语「聚集」动词，工业使它带上了技术含义。

latinIntro.en: The root simul, 'together', also gives similar and simultaneous.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 simul「一起」也派生出 similar 与 simultaneous。

definition_en: the act of taking something away or getting rid of it
core_image: 工人把旧招牌从墙上整个卸下来搬走
scene: 装修队第一件事就是把厨房那面旧瓷砖全部拆掉。 The first job of the builders was the removal of the old tiles in the kitchen.
sceneCN: 这里 removal 是「拆除、去除」（第 1 个义项：把某物拿走或清除）；句意：装修队的第一项工作就是把厨房的旧瓷砖拆掉。

derivatives.zh: removal 的动词来源，义为「移开；去除」
remove 加 -able 构成，义为「可拆卸的」

senses.title: The act of taking something away
senses.definition: the act of taking a thing from one place and putting it somewhere else or out of the way
senses.definitionCN: 把某物从一处拿走、移到别处或挪开的行为
senses.example: The removal of the old bridge took three months.
senses.exampleCN: 拆除旧桥花了三个月。
senses.why: Removal is simply the noun of remove, so the whole word restates the act of moving something away.
senses.whyCN: removal 就是 remove 的名词，整词只是重述「把东西移走」这个动作。

senses.title: The act of getting rid of something
senses.definition: the process of clearing away dirt, waste, or something unwanted
senses.definitionCN: 清除污渍、废物或不想要之物的过程
senses.example: Stain removal is easiest while the mark is still wet.
senses.exampleCN: 污渍还湿的时候最容易除掉。
senses.why: Taking a thing away and taking a stain away are the same motion, only the thing belongs to the surface.
senses.whyCN: 把东西拿走与把污渍去掉是同一个动作，只是对象附着在表面上。

senses.title: Dismissal from a post
senses.definition: the act of forcing someone out of a job or an official position
senses.definitionCN: 迫使某人离开职位或官方岗位的行为
senses.example: The board voted for the removal of the director.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会投票决定免去这位主管的职务。
senses.why: A person can be moved out of a post just as an object can be moved out of a room.
senses.whyCN: 人也可以像物件一样被移出职位，于是有了免职义。

senses.title: The act of moving to a new home
senses.definition: the process of carrying furniture and belongings to a different house or office
senses.definitionCN: 把家具和物品搬到另一处住宅或办公室的过程
senses.example: The removal to the new flat took a single weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 搬到新公寓只用了一个周末。
senses.why: Moving your own goods away from one address to another is the household version of the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 把自己的家当从一个地址搬到另一个地址，就是同一动词的家庭版。

intro.en: Removal is an English noun formed from the verb remove with the ending -al.
intro.cn: removal 是英语中由动词 remove 加名词词尾 -al 构成的名词。

items.en: Removere, from re- and movere, supplies the base meaning of moving away.
items.cn: 由 re- 与 movere 构成的 removere 提供了「移开」的基础意义。

items.en: Old French remouvoir gives English the verb remove.
items.cn: 古法语 remouvoir 给英语带来动词 remove。

items.en: The verb remove is recorded early in the sense of moving something away.
items.cn: 动词 remove 很早就以「移开某物」的意义被记录。

items.en: The noun removal appears with the ending -al, naming the act rather than the result.
items.cn: 十六世纪出现带 -al 的名词 removal，指行为本身而非结果。

items.en: The word spreads into house moving, waste collection, and dismissal from office.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到搬家、垃圾清运以及免职等领域。

note.en: Removal is the action noun of remove, and it stands beside words for clearing away and for dismissal.
note.cn: removal 是 remove 的动作名词，与表示清除和免职的词相邻。

entries.definitionCN: 移开；去除，是 removal 的动词

entries.definition: able to be taken off or out
a person or firm that moves furniture
entries.definitionCN: 搬家工人或搬家公司，多见于澳大利亚英语

entries.definition: the act of removing written or stored material
entries.definitionCN: 删除，多用于文字与数据

entries.definition: the act of clearing a space of unwanted things
the act of removing someone from a job
entries.definitionCN: 解雇；免职，与第三义项接近

normalIntro.en: Removal is remove plus the noun ending -al, so every hook starts from the verb.
normalIntro.cn: removal 就是 remove 加名词词尾 -al，所以记忆钩子都从动词出发。

normal.en: Drop the final e of remove and add -al: removal.
normal.cn: 去掉 remove 末尾的 e，加上 -al 就是 removal。

normal.en: The noun names an act, while the verb names the action itself.
normal.cn: 名词指行为过程，动词指去做这个动作。

normal.en: A removal van is the British phrase for a moving truck.
normal.cn: removal van 是英式英语里的「搬家货车」。

normal.en: The movere root of moving is still there under the prefix and endings.
normal.cn: 前缀与词尾之下仍藏着表示「移动」的 movere 词根。

normal.en: In law and politics, removal often means being forced out of office.
normal.cn: 在法律与政治语境中，removal 常指被免职。

abstract.en: Picture a sign being unscrewed and carried off a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一块招牌被拧下螺丝，从墙上搬走。

abstract.en: See a sponge lifting a dark mark off a white shirt.
abstract.cn: 想象海绵把白衬衫上的黑渍吸走。

abstract.en: Think of boxes stacked by a door on moving day.
abstract.cn: 想搬家那天门口堆起的纸箱。

examples.en: The removal of the tree changed the whole garden.
examples.cn: 那棵树被移走后，整个花园都变了样。

examples.en: They booked a removal company for the end of the month.
examples.cn: 他们预订了一家搬家公司，定在月底。

examples.en: The committee demanded the removal of the chairman.
examples.cn: 委员会要求罢免主席。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞木屋」——想象瑞丽的木屋被整间搬走，只剩空地；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 动词 remove 加名词词尾 -al 构成；remove 源自拉丁语 removere（re-「向后」+ movere「移动」）。

sensesIntro.en: One act of moving something away covers objects, dirt, people in posts, and whole households.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个「把东西移走」的动作，涵盖了物件、污垢、职位上的人以及整个家庭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a worn sign unscrewed and carried off the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：旧招牌被拧下螺丝，从墙上搬走。

branches.en: The physical taking away is the base act.
branches.cn: 物理上的拿走是基础动作。

branches.en: Clearing dirt away is the same act applied to a surface.
branches.cn: 清除污垢是同一动作施加在表面上。

branches.en: Moving a person out of a post applies it to a job.
branches.cn: 把一个人移出职位，是同一动作施加在岗位上。

branches.en: Moving a household applies it to a whole set of objects.
branches.cn: 搬家把这一动作施加于一整套物品。

branches.en: Both are movement of goods from one place to another.
branches.cn: 两者都是物品从一处到另一处的移动。

intro.en: Removal adds an English noun ending to a Latin-derived verb, so it shows two layers at once.
intro.cn: removal 在拉丁来源的动词上加了英语名词词尾，同时呈现两层来源。

latinIntro.en: The Latin prefix re- and the root movere, to move, still shape the word under its English ending.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁前缀 re- 与表示「移动」的词根 movere，在英语词尾之下仍然塑造着这个词。

items.example: Re- marks movement away from a place.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 标记离开某处的移动。

items.example: The mov- root is shared with motion.
items.exampleCN: mov- 词根与 motion 共用。

items.example: Movere is the verb behind remove.
items.exampleCN: movere 是 remove 背后的动词。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或过程的名词词尾
items.example: The ending -al turns remove into an act noun.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 把 remove 变成表示行为的抽象名词。

items.example: Removere is the Latin ancestor of the family.
items.exampleCN: removere 是这一词族的拉丁祖先。

items.example: Removable means able to be removed.
items.exampleCN: removable 意为「可以被拆下的」。

items.example: A removable cover makes cleaning easier.
items.exampleCN: 可拆卸的盖子让清洁更方便。

items.example: Motion keeps the plain movere root.
items.exampleCN: motion 保留了朴素的 movere 词根。

definition_en: lacking knowledge, or not aware of a particular fact
core_image: 一个人面对新机器，连开关都找不到
scene: 他并非懒惰，只是对这项技术完全不了解。 He was not lazy, only ignorant of the technology.
sceneCN: 这里 ignorant 是「无知的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他并非懒惰，只是对这项技术完全不了解。

senses.title: Lacking knowledge
senses.definition: having little knowledge or education
senses.definitionCN: 知识或教育不足的
senses.example: He was not lazy, only ignorant of the technology.
senses.exampleCN: 他并非懒惰，只是对这项技术完全不了解。
senses.why: This is the broad sense of lacking knowledge.
senses.whyCN: 这是缺乏知识的广义义项。

senses.title: Not aware
senses.definition: not knowing about a particular fact
senses.definitionCN: 不知道某一具体事实的
senses.example: They were ignorant of the danger ahead.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对前方的危险一无所知。
senses.why: Here only one fact is missing.
senses.whyCN: 这里只缺少一件具体事实。

intro.en: Ignorant is the Latin adjective for not knowing.
intro.cn: ignorant 是拉丁语中表示不知道的形容词。

items.en: Ignorans meant not knowing.
items.cn: ignorans 意为不知道的。

items.en: Ignorare meant not to know.
items.cn: ignorare 意为不知道。

items.en: Ignorant meant lacking knowledge.
items.cn: ignorant 意为缺乏知识的。

items.en: Ignorant described a person without knowledge.
items.cn: ignorant 形容没有知识的人。

items.en: Ignorant also means not aware of a fact.
items.cn: ignorant 也指不知情。

note.en: Ignorant is compared with look-alike words and with words for lacking knowledge.
note.cn: 把 ignorant 与形近词以及表示无知的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Ignorant describes a person on the outside of a piece of knowledge.
normalIntro.cn: ignorant 描述站在某项知识之外的人。

normal.en: He was ignorant of the new rule.
normal.cn: 他不知道这条新规定。

normal.en: They were ignorant of the danger ahead.
normal.cn: 他们对前方的危险一无所知。

normal.en: Do not confuse ignorant with stupid.
normal.cn: 别把无知和愚蠢混为一谈。

normal.en: She felt ignorant among the experts.
normal.cn: 在专家中间她感到自己无知。

normal.en: No one should remain ignorant of the law.
normal.cn: 没有人应当对法律一无所知。

abstract.en: Ignorant is a position, not a permanent nature.
abstract.cn: 无知是一种位置，而非永恒的本性。

abstract.en: We are all ignorant of most things.
abstract.cn: 对大多数事物我们都很无知。

abstract.en: The honest answer is often that we are ignorant.
abstract.cn: 诚实的回答常常是我们不知道。

examples.en: He was not lazy, only ignorant of the technology.
examples.cn: 他并非懒惰，只是对这项技术完全不了解。

examples.en: They were ignorant of the danger ahead.
examples.cn: 他们对前方的危险一无所知。

examples.en: No one should remain ignorant of the law.
examples.cn: 没有人应当对法律一无所知。

dict_mnemonic.note: 词根记忆 · ignor（不知道）+ -ant（形容词）
dict_mnemonic.text: ignor 来自拉丁语 ignorare（不知道），-ant 构成形容词，ignorant 就是「不知道的、无知的、不知情的」。

root: 来自拉丁语 ignorans（不知道的），源于 ignorare（不知道）。

sensesIntro.en: Ignorant means lacking knowledge or not aware of a fact.
sensesIntro.cn: ignorant 表示缺乏知识或不知情。

core.en: Standing outside a piece of knowledge.
core.cn: 站在一项知识之外。

branches.en: He was ignorant of the new rule.
branches.cn: 他不知道这条新规定。

branches.en: She felt ignorant among the experts.
branches.cn: 在专家中间她感到自己无知。

branches.en: They were ignorant of the danger ahead.
branches.cn: 他们对前方的危险一无所知。

branches.en: One missing fact can make a person ignorant.
branches.cn: 缺少一件事实就能让人不知情。

branches.en: Do not confuse ignorant with stupid.
branches.cn: 别把无知和愚蠢混为一谈。

intro.en: Ignorant is the adjective beside ignorance and ignore.
intro.cn: ignorant 是 ignorance 与 ignore 旁边的形容词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin verb ignorare, not to know, underlies all three.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语动词 ignorare（不知道）支撑着这三个词。

items.example: He is ignorant of the facts.
They were unaware of the risk.

latinEntries.example: Ignorans is the source of ignorant.
latinEntries.exampleCN: ignorans 是 ignorant 的来源。

definition_en: in the way that is usual for a person, place or kind of thing
core_image: 一份日程表上几乎每天都相同的时刻
scene: 办公室的时钟指向下午，茶水间又排起了队。 Typically, the lift is slowest just after lunch.
sceneCN: 这里 typically 是「通常；一般说来」（第 1 个义项：按该类事物常见的做法）；句意为午饭刚过电梯照例最慢。日程表上几乎每天相同的时刻，就是这个词的样子。

derivatives.zh: 由 typically 去掉 -ly 的原形，义为「典型的」
由同一词干加 -ity 构成，义为「典型性」
由 typically 加否定前缀 a- 构成，义为「非典型地」

senses.title: As a rule
senses.definition: in the way that usually happens
senses.definitionCN: 按通常会发生的方式
senses.example: Typically, the lift is slowest just after lunch.
senses.exampleCN: 午饭刚过，电梯照例最慢。
senses.why: The adverb generalises: what is true of the type is expected of the case.
senses.whyCN: 副词做的是普遍化：类型如此，具体一例便可预期如此。

senses.title: In a way that represents
senses.definition: in a way that clearly shows the character of a group
senses.definitionCN: 以清楚体现某群体特征的方式
senses.example: The village looks typically Mediterranean.
senses.exampleCN: 这村子看上去是典型的地中海风格。
senses.why: Instead of pointing at frequency, this use points at how well a feature stands for its class.
senses.whyCN: 这一用法不指向出现频率，而指向某特征代表其类别的贴切程度。

intro.en: Typically is the adverb of typical, carrying the Greek stamp of typos with it.
intro.cn: typically 是 typical 的副词，也带着希腊语 typos 那个印。

items.en: Typos meant a blow and the mark it leaves on a surface.
items.cn: typos 意为击打及其在表面留下的印。

items.en: Typicus gave the adjective; the adverb needed only the English ending -ly.
items.cn: typic(us) 给出形容词，副词只需加英语词尾 -ly。

items.en: Typical appeared first, and typically followed in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: typical 先出现，typically 在十八世纪跟上。

items.en: Writers used it to sum up a habit in one word.
items.cn: 作家用它以一个词概括一种常态。

items.en: Today it opens sentences as a ready-made comment.
items.cn: 今天它常放在句首，作为现成的评语。

note.en: The first group holds adverbs of frequency, the second holds the matching adjective forms.
note.cn: 第一组是频度副词，第二组是对应的形容词。

entries.definition: In a way that marks the person.

normalIntro.en: Typically is typical plus -ly, doing the work of usually with a classier air.
normalIntro.cn: typically 是 typical 加 -ly，做的正是 usually 的活，只是更文雅。

normal.en: Drop -ly and you have the adjective typical.
normal.cn: 去掉 -ly 就是形容词 typical。

normal.en: Coming first in a sentence, it gives a wry comment.
normal.cn: 放在句首时，常带一点无奈的评语意味。

normal.en: Typically before a number means on average.
normal.cn: 在数字前表示平均而言。

normal.en: Compared with usually, it points at the type.
normal.cn: 比起 usually，它更指向「这一类」。

normal.en: The stress stays on the first syllable: TYP-ically.
normal.cn: 重音仍在第一音节。

abstract.en: A clock showing the same time every day.
abstract.cn: 每天都指向同一时刻的钟。

abstract.en: A queue forming at the same door each noon.
abstract.cn: 每天中午在同一扇门前排起的队。

abstract.en: A red roof repeated along one street.
abstract.cn: 一条街上重复出现的红屋顶。

examples.en: Typically, the meeting lasts about forty minutes.
examples.cn: 这种会议通常持续四十分钟左右。

examples.en: The house is typically English, with a small garden.
examples.cn: 这房子是典型的英式，还带个小花园。

examples.en: Such storms typically pass within a day.
examples.cn: 这类风暴一般一天之内就过去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「提皮扣里」——一提皮扣就能从里翻出代表，典型得很。

root: 由 typical（典型的）加副词词尾 -ly 构成，而 typical 源自希腊语 typos（一击、印痕），本义为按该类特征的样子，同族词有 typical、typicality。

sensesIntro.en: First how things usually go, then how well a case stands for its class.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是事物通常怎样，再是一例怎样代表它那一类。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a schedule repeating the same hour.
core.cn: 核心意象：日程表重复着同一时刻。

branches.en: The rule branch: what usually happens.
branches.cn: 规则分支：通常发生的事。

branches.en: The sample branch: a case that shows the type.
branches.cn: 样本分支：显出类别的例子。

branches.en: The average branch: a figure for the whole.
branches.cn: 平均分支：整体给出的数字。

branches.en: The judgement branch: often said with a raised brow.
branches.cn: 评价分支：常带着挑眉的语气。

branches.en: The habit branch: repetition becomes character.
branches.cn: 习惯分支：重复成了性格。

intro.en: Typically is a root with -ical and -ly stacked on it, a good example of English layering.
intro.cn: typically 是词根上叠了 -ical 与 -ly，正好展示英语的层层相加。

latinIntro.en: The Latin adjective typicus supports the stem, listed below.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁形容词 typicus 支撑着这个词干，列在下面。

definition_zh: 不愿意的；勉强的；不情愿的；不肯的
definition_en: not wanting to do something, and doing it only with reluctance
core_image: 脚往前挪，身子却往后拽
scene: 孩子被叫去道歉，手扶着门框迟迟不肯松开。 He was unwilling to admit that the mistake was his.
sceneCN: 这里 unwilling 是「不愿意的」（第 1 个义项：心里不想做）；句意为他怎么也不肯承认这错在自己。脚往前、身子后拽的画面，正是这个词的核心。

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「不情愿地」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不愿；勉强」
去掉否定前缀后的肯定形式，义为「乐意的」
同源名词，义为「意志；意愿」

senses.title: Not wanting to do something
senses.definition: not wanting to do a thing that one has been asked to do
senses.definitionCN: 对别人要求做的事心里并不想做
senses.example: He was unwilling to lend the car to anyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他不愿意把车借给任何人。
senses.why: The prefix says not and the base says having the will for something, so the word names a will that is absent.
senses.whyCN: 前缀表示「不」，词根表示「对某事有意愿」，因此这个词说的是「意愿缺位」。

senses.title: Doing it, but with resistance
senses.definition: doing something anyway, though clearly against one's wish
senses.definitionCN: 虽然做了，但明显违背自己的意愿
senses.example: The witness gave an unwilling answer.
senses.exampleCN: 证人勉强给出了回答。
senses.why: When the will is absent but the act happens anyway, the act carries the resistance inside it.
senses.whyCN: 意愿缺位而事情照样做了，这份抵触就留在了动作里。

senses.title: A role taken on without choice
senses.definition: used of people who are in a situation and never chose it
senses.definitionCN: 形容身处其中而从未自己选择的人
senses.example: He became an unwilling leader when the captain fell ill.
senses.exampleCN: 队长病倒后，他成了不情愿的领头人。
senses.why: A person who never wanted the part is still inside it, so the word comes to name the role itself.
senses.whyCN: 从没想要这个位置的人却仍身在其中，于是这个词也用来指这个角色。

senses.title: A refusal to accept a fact
senses.definition: used of refusal to admit or accept something true
senses.definitionCN: 形容不愿意承认或接受某个事实
senses.example: She was unwilling to believe the letter was real.
senses.exampleCN: 她不肯相信那封信是真的。
senses.why: Not wanting to act turns into not wanting to see, and the object of the will becomes a fact.
senses.whyCN: 不想做会转为不想看见，意愿的对象于是变成了一个事实。

senses.title: Slow response because of doubt
senses.definition: used of a slow or hesitant response that shows no enthusiasm
senses.definitionCN: 形容因犹疑而显得没有热情的反应
senses.example: There was an unwilling silence before he answered.
senses.exampleCN: 他回答之前有一段不太情愿的沉默。
senses.why: A will that pulls back shows in timing, so the word also describes answers that come late.
senses.whyCN: 退缩的意愿会从快慢上看出来，因此这个词也形容迟迟才到的回应。

intro.en: A native negative prefix on an adjective made from the old noun for will.
intro.cn: 本土否定前缀压在一个由古老的「意愿」名词构成的形容词上。

items.en: The prefix un- is native and negates a quality directly.
items.cn: 前缀 un- 为英语本土成分，直接否定某一性质。

items.en: The noun willa meant wish or desire, and willan meant to want.
items.cn: 名词 willa 意为「愿望」，动词 willan 意为「想要」。

items.en: The adjectives willing and unwilling are formed with the suffix -ing on will.
items.cn: 形容词 willing 与 unwilling 由 will 加词尾 -ing 构成。

items.en: Unwilling is fixed in the frame be unwilling to do, common in reports and statements.
items.cn: unwilling 固定在 be unwilling to do 这一框架中，常见于报告与陈述。

items.en: The noun unwillingness and the adverb unwillingly follow as regular forms.
items.cn: 随后按规律产生了名词 unwillingness 与副词 unwillingly。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the will family, while the near-meaning group collects words of reluctance and refusal.
note.cn: 形近组沿 will 词族展开，近义组汇集表示不情愿与拒绝的说法。

entries.definition: the power to decide or want

entries.definitionCN: 野生的（只是拼写相近，词源不同）

normalIntro.en: The word is built on the ordinary noun for the will, with a negative prefix and a participle ending.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建在日常表示「意愿」的名词上，前面加否定前缀，后面加分词词尾。

normal.en: Un- plus willing: willing goes back to will, the wish to act.
normal.cn: un- 加 willing：willing 源自 will，即行动的愿望。

normal.en: Be unwilling to do is the frame to learn first.
normal.cn: be unwilling to do 是最先要记住的框架。

normal.en: An unwilling helper is someone who helps and resents it.
normal.cn: an unwilling helper 指帮了忙却满腹怨气的人。

normal.en: Unwilling is about will; reluctant is about hesitation of feeling.
normal.cn: unwilling 重在意愿，reluctant 重在情绪上的迟疑。

normal.en: The noun is unwillingness, the adverb unwillingly.
normal.cn: 名词是 unwillingness，副词是 unwillingly。

abstract.en: Watch feet step forward while the body leans back.
abstract.cn: 想象脚往前迈，身子却向后仰。

abstract.en: See a hand hold the door frame and not let go.
abstract.cn: 看见一只手扶着门框不肯松。

abstract.en: Hear an answer given a beat too late.
abstract.cn: 听一句慢了一拍的回答。

examples.en: The company was unwilling to change its rules.
examples.cn: 公司不愿更改自己的规定。

examples.en: An unwilling smile crossed his face when the bill arrived.
examples.cn: 账单送来时，他脸上掠过一丝勉强的笑。

examples.en: She unwillingly handed over the letter and left the room.
examples.cn: 她不情愿地交出那封信，离开了房间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺不灵」——嘴上被派了活儿，心里觉得俺不灵，干脆就不愿意干。

root: 英语本土构词：前缀 un-（不）+ willing（愿意的），willing 由 will（意愿；意志）加 -ing 构成，will 可追溯至古英语 willa / willan（愿望、想要）

sensesIntro.en: One missing will shows up as refusal, as grudging compliance, as a forced role, and as slow doubt.
sensesIntro.cn: 一份缺席的意愿，表现为拒绝、勉强照办、被迫担当与迟疑拖沓。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: feet moving forward while the body pulls back.
core.cn: 核心意象：脚往前挪，身子往后拽。

branches.en: The plain branch: the wish to do it is simply absent.
branches.cn: 朴素分支：想做的念头根本没有。

branches.en: The grudging branch: the act is done, the mood is not.
branches.cn: 勉强分支：事做了，情绪不在。

branches.en: The role branch: people placed where they never chose.
branches.cn: 角色分支：被放进从未选择的位置。

branches.en: The denial branch: a truth that will not be admitted.
branches.cn: 否认分支：不愿承认的事实。

branches.en: The hesitation branch: an answer that arrives late.
branches.cn: 迟疑分支：迟迟才到的回答。

intro.en: A native negative prefix and a very old suffix sit on the noun for the will.
intro.cn: 本土否定前缀与一个古老的词尾都压在表示「意愿」的名词上。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic; the Latin verb for wishing is velle, whose noun is voluntas.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语；拉丁语中表示意愿的动词是 velle，名词为 voluntas。

items.example: She lost the will to argue.

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀

definition_zh: 集会；拉力赛；集合重整；回升
definition_en: a large public meeting in support of a cause; a long-distance motor race; to bring people together again after a setback; to recover strength or value after a fall
core_image: 广场上举着标语的人群与一阵紧似一阵的鼓声
scene: 广场上人群举着标语，鼓声一阵接一阵，队伍在雨里也没有散。 Thousands joined the rally in the square despite the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 rally 是「集会」（第 1 个义项：为某个主张而举行的大型公众集会）；句意为尽管下着雨，仍有数千人参加了广场上的集会。画面里可留意：标语牌、鼓声、雨中不散的人群。

pos.zh: 集会；拉力赛；（力量或价格）回升

derivatives.zh: rally 加 -ing，指重新集结或争取支持的过程
rally 加 -ist，指参加汽车拉力赛的人
与 rally 同源，指结盟的伙伴或同盟国

senses.title: A large public meeting
senses.definition: a large gathering of people who share a cause or a demand
senses.definitionCN: 为共同主张或诉求而聚集的大批人群
senses.example: Thousands joined the rally in the square.
senses.exampleCN: 数千人参加了广场上的集会。
senses.why: The French verb meant to unite again, and a rally is literally a gathering of people who have come back together.
senses.whyCN: 那个法语动词意为重新联合，而 rally 字面上就是「重新聚到一起」的人群。

senses.title: A long-distance motor race
senses.definition: a car competition run over public roads or rough ground, often for several days
senses.definitionCN: 在公路或崎岖地面上进行、常持续数日的汽车比赛
senses.example: He entered a three-day rally across the mountains.
senses.exampleCN: 他参加了一场为期三天的山地拉力赛。
senses.why: A rally brings vehicles together from stage to stage, and the name kept the idea of gathering at checkpoints.
senses.whyCN: 拉力赛把车辆一站一站地聚到一起，这个名字保留了「在检查点集合」的意思。

senses.title: To bring people together again
senses.definition: to gather people or forces after a defeat or a setback
senses.definitionCN: 在失败或挫折之后把人或力量重新聚集起来
senses.example: The team rallied after losing the first set.
senses.exampleCN: 球队在输掉第一局后重整旗鼓。
senses.why: The core sense is to reunite what has scattered, and sport and politics both use it for recovery after a loss.
senses.whyCN: 核心意思是把散开的东西重新联合起来，体育与政治都用它表示失败后的恢复。

senses.title: To recover strength or value
senses.definition: to regain strength, health or market value after a decline
senses.definitionCN: 在下降之后重新获得力量、健康或市场价值
senses.example: Shares rallied after the announcement.
senses.exampleCN: 消息公布后股价回升。
senses.why: A group that reunites becomes stronger, and in markets a price that gathers itself again is said to rally.
senses.whyCN: 重新联合起来的群体变得更强，在市场上，一个重新聚拢的价格也被称为 rally。

intro.en: Rally comes from a French verb meaning to unite again, built on the Latin verb for binding, and it reached English through warfare and politics.
intro.cn: rally 来自一个意为「重新联合」的法语动词，建立在拉丁语表示「捆绑」的动词上，并经战争与政治进入英语。

items.en: Ligare meant to bind or to tie together, the root of words about alliance and obligation.
items.cn: ligare 意为捆绑、系在一起，是表示结盟与义务的一族词的根。

items.en: Allier meant to unite or to join, and its Latin base carried the image of things tied into one bundle.
items.cn: allier 意为联合、结合，其拉丁语基础带有「把东西捆成一束」的形象。

items.en: Rallier added the prefix of return, so it meant to gather again people who had scattered.
items.cn: rallier 加上了表示「返回」的前缀，意为把散开的人重新聚集起来。

items.en: A rally was first a regrouping of troops after confusion, and the word kept that sense of recovering order.
items.cn: rally 最初指混乱之后重新集结部队，这个词保留了「恢复秩序」的意味。

items.en: Modern English uses rally for a public meeting, for a motor race, for regrouping and for recovering strength or price.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rally 指公众集会、汽车赛、重新集结，以及力量或价格的恢复。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms of the same stem; the near-meaning group gathers words for gatherings and recovery.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词干上的形式；近义组收表示聚会与恢复的词。

entries.definition: The act of gathering support or regrouping.
entries.definitionCN: 争取支持或重新集结的行为。

entries.definition: A driver who takes part in rallies.
A partner joined to another for a common purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 为共同目的与他人结盟的伙伴。

entries.definition: A group of people meeting together.
A public protest or show of support.
entries.definitionCN: 公开的抗议或支持展示。

entries.definition: To return to a former state after difficulty.
entries.definitionCN: 困难之后回到原来的状态。

entries.definition: To bring something back to strength or life.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物恢复力量或活力。

normalIntro.en: The word means to gather again: people, troops, a team, a price, or a field of cars.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词意为「重新聚拢」：人群、军队、队伍、价格，或一整个赛场的车辆。

normal.en: Rally and ally share the Latin verb for binding, because a rally ties people back together.
normal.cn: rally 与 ally 共用拉丁语表示捆绑的动词，因为集会把人重新系在一起。

normal.en: Rally round is the phrase for friends gathering to support someone in trouble.
normal.cn: rally round 指朋友聚拢过来支持陷入困境的人。

normal.en: A political rally gathers supporters, while a car rally gathers vehicles at checkpoints.
normal.cn: 政治集会聚集支持者，汽车拉力赛把车辆聚集在检查点。

normal.en: Shares rally when prices regain ground after a fall, as if the market had regrouped.
normal.cn: 股价在下跌后回升时叫 rally，仿佛市场重新集结了。

normal.en: Rally the team means lift their spirits after a defeat, not merely call them together.
normal.cn: rally the team 指在失败后提振士气，而不只是把人叫到一起。

abstract.en: A rally is a crowd that decides to feel the same thing at the same time.
abstract.cn: 集会是一群决定在同一时间感受同一件事的人。

abstract.en: Recovering after a loss is a kind of reunion with yourself, which is why the word serves sport and markets alike.
abstract.cn: 失败后的恢复是与自己的一次重逢，所以这个词既适用于体育，也适用于市场。

abstract.en: What gathers can scatter again, and the word quietly warns that recovery is a process, not a state.
abstract.cn: 聚起来的东西还会再散开，这个词悄悄提醒：恢复是一个过程，而不是一种状态。

examples.en: The rally ended with a short speech and a song.
examples.cn: 集会在一段简短演讲和一首歌中结束。

examples.en: He drove in his first rally when he was nineteen.
examples.cn: 他十九岁时参加了第一场拉力赛。

examples.en: The village rallied round to rebuild the damaged school.
examples.cn: 全村人团结起来重建受损的学校。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「瑞利」——人群锐利地聚到一处，越聚越有力量，记住 rally 是集会、重整。

root: 拉丁语 ligare（捆绑）→ 法语 allier（联合）→ rallier（重新聚集）→ 英语 rally；同族有 ally、alliance、rallying。

sensesIntro.en: The core is gathering again; the senses divide into a public meeting, a motor race of stages, regrouping after a loss and recovering strength or value.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「重新聚拢」；义项分为公众集会、分段进行的汽车赛、失败后的重整，以及力量或价格的恢复。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a crowd with banners in a square, drums sounding through the rain.
core.cn: 核心意象：广场上举着标语的人群，鼓声穿过雨幕。

chain: A RACE FROM STAGE TO STAGE

branches.en: banners held above a wet square
branches.cn: 湿广场上方举起的标语

branches.en: cars waiting at a checkpoint
branches.cn: 在检查点等候的赛车

branches.en: a team standing closer after a loss
branches.cn: 失败后站得更近的队伍

branches.en: a price line turning upward
branches.cn: 掉头向上的价格线

branches.en: the same regrouping, once of cars and once of people
branches.cn: 同一种重新集结，一次是车辆，一次是人

intro.en: The word came through French from the Latin verb for binding, and English adds endings for activities and people.
intro.cn: 这个词经法语来自拉丁语表示捆绑的动词，英语加上表示活动与人的词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin ligare also stands behind ally and alliance, which keep the idea of being tied together.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ligare 也支撑着 ally 与 alliance，它们保留了「被系在一起」的意思。

definition_en: a fault that makes something imperfect; also to leave one's country or group for another
core_image: 新杯子对着光一转，杯壁上现出一道细纹
scene: 质检员把杯子举到灯下，慢慢转了一圈，忽然停住了手。 The inspector found a defect in the glass.
sceneCN: 这里 defect 指「缺陷」（第 1 个义项：产品上的瑕疵）；句意是质检员在这只玻璃杯上发现了瑕疵。

senses.title: A fault in a made thing
senses.definition: a small fault that spoils the working of a product
senses.definitionCN: 使产品不能正常使用的小毛病
senses.example: The inspector found a defect in the glass.
senses.exampleCN: 质检员在这只玻璃杯上发现了缺陷。
senses.why: A flaw shows itself only when the light is right.
senses.whyCN: 瑕疵只有在光线对的时候才露出来。

senses.title: A weakness in a person or plan
senses.definition: a weakness in character, argument or arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 性格、论证或安排上的薄弱之处
senses.example: There is one defect in your argument.
senses.exampleCN: 你的论证里有一处漏洞。
senses.why: What breaks a thing is the same whatever the thing is.
senses.whyCN: 弄坏东西的那个原因，放在哪儿都一样。

senses.title: Leave one side for another
senses.definition: to abandon one's country or group and join the opposite side
senses.definitionCN: 离开自己的国家或团体，投向对立一方
senses.example: He defected to the neighbouring country in secret.
senses.exampleCN: 他秘密叛逃到了邻国。
senses.why: A person with a crack in loyalty simply walks away.
senses.whyCN: 忠诚上有了裂缝的人，就抬脚走开了。

intro.en: Defect comes from Latin deficere, to fail or desert, built from de- away and facere to do.
intro.cn: defect 来自拉丁语 deficere（做不好、离开），由 de-（离开）与 facere（做）组成。

items.en: Deficere meant to be lacking or to fall away from a duty.
items.cn: deficere 意为缺少，或从职守上退开。

items.en: Defectus named a gap, a failure or a desertion.
items.cn: defectus 指缺口、失误或背离。

items.en: English took it first as a noun for something missing.
items.cn: 英语先把它作名词，指缺失的东西。

items.en: The verb appeared with the sense of deserting a side.
items.cn: 动词用法出现，意思是背弃一方。

items.en: Today a defect is mostly a fault found in goods, plans or eyes.
items.cn: 如今 defect 多指货物、方案或眼睛上的毛病。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the defe- opening, and the meaning group names one fault in three ways.
note.cn: 形近组共用 defe- 开头，近义组则用三种说法讲同一种毛病。

entries.definition: a mark or weakness that spoils something
entries.definitionCN: 破坏事物的瑕疵或弱点

entries.definition: a mistake or a bad part in something
a failure to reach a good standard
entries.definitionCN: 未能达到应有水准之处

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a crack seen against the light and end with a man quietly changing sides.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从对着光看见的一道裂纹开始，落到一个人悄悄换了阵营。

normal.en: A perfect cup is silent; a cracked one rings differently.
normal.cn: 完好的杯子不出声，裂了的敲起来音不一样。

normal.en: Every argument has one place where it gives way.
normal.cn: 每个论证都有一处会松口的地方。

normal.en: A gap in a wall is small, but that is where the wind comes in.
normal.cn: 墙上的缝不大，风偏偏从那进。

normal.en: A soldier who leaves his post is the same word as a broken part.
normal.cn: 离开岗位的士兵，和坏掉的零件共用一个词。

normal.en: De-fect: something not done, and so not whole.
normal.cn: de-fect 拆开看，就是「没做全」，所以不完整。

abstract.en: Picture a thin line in glass that catches the light for a second.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃里一条细线，只闪了一下光。

abstract.en: Picture a key that almost turns but never quite does.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙，差一点就能转动。

abstract.en: Picture a coat left on a chair by someone who is not coming back.
abstract.cn: 想象一件外套留在椅子上，主人不再回来。

examples.en: The inspector found a defect in the glass.
examples.cn: 质检员在这只玻璃杯上发现了缺陷。

examples.en: This model was returned because of a design defect.
examples.cn: 这款因为设计缺陷被退了回来。

examples.en: There is one defect in your argument.
examples.cn: 你的论证里有一处漏洞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 defect 记成「得废」：de 开头，fect 听着像「废掉」，东西一废，就是有缺陷。

root: 源自拉丁语 deficere（缺少、背离），由 de-（离开）与 facere（做）合成，名词 defectus 指缺口与背离。英语先借作名词表示缺失，十六世纪又生出「叛逃」的动词义，两条线都从「离开本该在的位置」长出来。

sensesIntro.en: From a crack in a cup, to a hole in an argument, to a man who walks to the other side.
sensesIntro.cn: 从杯子上的裂纹，到论证里的漏洞，再到走到对面去的那个人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin crack that only shows in the right light.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道只在合适光线下才显出的细纹。

branches.en: The first sense is a fault inside a finished product.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是成品内部的一处毛病。

branches.en: The same missing piece, in reasoning and in character, is a weakness.
branches.cn: 同样的缺失放到论证和性格上，就是弱点。

branches.en: A person who lacks loyalty simply leaves his own side.
branches.cn: 少了忠诚的人，就直接离开自己这一方。

branches.en: Objects and arguments both fail at the point where something is absent.
branches.cn: 物件和论证都是在缺了一块的地方出问题。

branches.en: Both senses describe a place where the whole can no longer be trusted.
branches.cn: 两个义项都指整体不再可靠的那一处。

intro.en: Defect forms adjectives of being faulty and nouns for the act of deserting.
intro.cn: defect 可派生出表示有毛病的形容词，也有表示背弃的名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is facere, to do, with de- meaning away or down.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁词基是 facere（做），前缀 de- 表示离开或向下。

items.example: The defect was easy to see.
items.exampleCN: 这个缺陷很容易看出来。

items.example: The shop replaced the defective lamp.
items.exampleCN: 店里换掉了那盏有毛病的灯。
这台机器的线路接得有毛病。

items.meaning: the act of leaving one's side
items.exampleCN: 他的叛逃让党内大为震动。

items.example: The defector crossed the border at night.
items.exampleCN: 那名叛逃者夜里越过了边境。
有瑕疵的货物可以退换。

items.example: The test shows a mild visual defect.
items.exampleCN: 检查显示有轻度视力缺陷。

items.meaning: a goal of no faults at all
items.example: The factory aims at zero defect.

definition_en: a continuous dull pain, or to feel such a pain
core_image: 一条酸胀的腿，疼得不尖，却一直不肯停
scene: 开了整天车，他的后背一直隐隐作痛。 His back ached after the long drive.
sceneCN: 这里的 ache 是「隐隐作痛」（第 2 个义项：持续性的身体疼痛）；句意是长途开车后他背疼。

derivatives.zh: 由现在分词转化而来，义为「疼痛的；令人心酸的」
由名词加形容词后缀构成，义为「酸痛的」
由 head 与 ache 复合而成，义为「头痛」

senses.title: A dull continuous pain
senses.definition: a pain that is not sharp but continues for a long time
senses.definitionCN: 不尖锐、却持续很久的疼痛
senses.example: She felt a dull ache in her knee.
senses.exampleCN: 她膝盖里有一阵钝钝的痛。
senses.why: Old English acan named a lasting bodily hurt rather than a sudden stab, so the noun keeps that slow, heavy quality.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 acan 指的是持续的身体疼痛，而不是突然的一刺，所以这个名词保留了那种缓慢、沉闷的性质。

senses.title: To hurt without stopping
senses.definition: to feel a steady dull pain in part of the body
senses.definitionCN: 身体某处持续地闷痛
senses.example: My legs ached after the long climb.
senses.exampleCN: 长途爬坡后我的腿一直酸痛。
senses.why: The same Old English verb simply turns the noun into an action: the body is doing the hurting, not holding a thing called pain.
senses.whyCN: 同一个古英语动词把名词变成动作：是身体在痛，而不是手里握着一个叫「痛」的东西。

senses.title: To long for something
senses.definition: to want something so much that it feels like a pain
senses.definitionCN: 极其想要某物，想要到像疼一样
senses.example: He ached to see his family again.
senses.exampleCN: 他渴望再见到家人。
senses.why: Emotional longing borrows the body's vocabulary: the heart hurts in the same dull way as an overtired leg.
senses.whyCN: 情感上的想念借用了身体的词：心口的闷痛，和过度劳累的腿是同一种钝法。

intro.en: The word is native English, old and Germanic, though its spelling was later reshaped.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语本土的古老日耳曼词，只是拼写后来被改过。

items.en: a reconstructed root meant to hurt or to be sore.
items.cn: 一个重构词根意为疼痛、酸痛。

items.en: acan was the verb to hurt, and the noun was spelt with a k.
items.cn: acan 是表示疼痛的动词，当时名词拼写里带 k。

items.en: ake served as both noun and verb in everyday speech.
items.cn: 在中古英语里，ake 同时作名词和动词使用。

items.en: writers respelt it ache, influenced by a Greek word for pain.
items.cn: 十六世纪的写作者把它改拼为 ache，受了希腊语中表示疼痛的词影响。

items.en: the verb now also expresses longing, as in ache to see someone.
items.cn: 如今这个动词也表达渴望，如 ache to see someone。

note.en: The first group shares the ache spelling; the second is other words for pain.
note.cn: 第一组共享 ache 这个拼写；第二组是别的表示疼痛的词。

entries.definition: giving or feeling a dull pain
to beat with a strong regular pain
the state of being tender and painful

normalIntro.en: The word is short, old and native, with a spelling changed by scholars.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词短、老、土生土长，只是拼写被学者改过一次。

normal.en: the old verb was acan, and the k sound survives in the pronunciation.
normal.cn: 古时的动词是 acan，那个 k 的音还留在读音里。

normal.en: the ch spelling came from a Greek word for pain, not from the root.
normal.cn: 拼写里的 ch 来自希腊语的「痛」，并不来自本词词根。

normal.en: headache and toothache show how productively ache builds compounds.
normal.cn: headache 与 toothache 显示 ache 构成复合词的能力。

normal.en: ache for is the fixed pattern for longing.
normal.cn: ache for 是表示渴望的固定搭配。

normal.en: the adjective aching often describes both legs and hearts.
normal.cn: 形容词 aching 既形容腿，也形容心。

abstract.en: Feel a heavy tiredness settling deep in the calves.
abstract.cn: 想象小腿深处压着一团沉沉的酸胀。

abstract.en: Picture a tooth that throbs with every heartbeat.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗牙随着每次心跳抽痛。

abstract.en: Think of a long absence that hurts like a bruise.
abstract.cn: 想象长久的离别像淤青一样发疼。

examples.en: A dull ache spread through her shoulders.
examples.cn: 一阵钝痛在她肩头蔓延。

examples.en: His knees ache whenever the weather turns cold.
examples.cn: 每逢天气转冷，他的膝盖就疼。

examples.en: She ached for a quiet room and an hour of sleep.
examples.cn: 她渴望一间安静的屋子和一小时的睡眠。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诶克」——疼得直喊「诶」，可这痛又不肯克止，一直闷着。

root: 古英语 acan（疼痛），源自日耳曼语系；本义是持续的身体疼痛，后引申为心里的渴望。拼写中的 ch 是十六世纪受希腊语 akhos（痛）影响而后加的。

sensesIntro.en: The same dull hurt runs through the noun, the verb and the longing heart.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一种钝钝的痛，贯穿名词、动词与渴望的心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a low steady hurt that will not switch off.
core.cn: 核心意象：一直关不掉的低声疼痛。

branches.en: the ache named as a thing
branches.cn: 被当作事物命名的隐痛

branches.en: the body doing the hurting
branches.cn: 身体正在发痛

branches.en: wanting someone until it hurts
branches.cn: 想一个人想到发疼

branches.en: noun and verb for the same steady sensation
branches.cn: 名词与动词指同一种持续感觉

branches.en: pain that moves from limbs to heart
branches.cn: 从四肢移到心口的痛

intro.en: This is a native Germanic word, so its parts are old English pieces rather than Latin ones.
intro.cn: 这是本土日耳曼词，所以它的构件是古英语部件，而不是拉丁部件。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor; the ch spelling was borrowed from Greek akhos by Renaissance writers.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有拉丁语祖先；拼写里的 ch 是文艺复兴时期的写作者从希腊语 akhos 借来的。

definition_en: a serious lack of food over a wide area, or a severe shortage of something
core_image: 干裂的土地上，空荡的粮仓和排队领粥的人群
scene: 连年干旱后，村庄陷入饥荒。 After years of drought, the village faced famine.
sceneCN: 这里 famine 是「饥荒」（第 1 个义项）；句意：连年干旱后，村庄面临饥荒。

senses.title: Widespread starvation
senses.definition: a serious lack of food over a wide area, causing many deaths
senses.definitionCN: 大范围严重缺粮，导致大量死亡
senses.example: The famine killed thousands of people.
senses.exampleCN: 这场饥荒夺去了数千人的生命。
senses.why: The core sense is mass hunger caused by missing food.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是食物短缺造成的大规模饥饿。

senses.title: Hunger and food shortage
senses.definition: the state of being extremely hungry because food is unavailable
senses.definitionCN: 因没有食物而极度饥饿的状态
senses.example: The animals died during the winter famine.
senses.exampleCN: 动物在冬季缺粮时死去。
senses.why: The event is felt as hunger by those inside it.
senses.whyCN: 身处其中的人把这一事件感受为饥饿。

senses.title: Severe shortage
senses.definition: an extreme scarcity of something other than food
senses.definitionCN: 除食物之外某物的极度稀缺
senses.example: Critics spoke of a famine of good ideas.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者谈到好想法的严重匮乏。
senses.why: The image of empty granaries extends to other shortages.
senses.whyCN: 空粮仓的意象扩展到其他短缺。

intro.en: Famine comes from Latin fames, hunger, through Old French famine.
intro.cn: famine 经古法语 famine 源自拉丁语 fames（饥饿）。

items.en: Fames means hunger.
items.cn: fames 意为饥饿。

items.en: Famelicus means hungry or starving.
items.cn: famelicus 意为饥饿的、挨饿的。

items.en: Famine named a great shortage of food.
items.cn: famine 指严重的食物短缺。

items.en: Famine entered English as widespread starvation.
items.cn: famine 以大范围饥荒之义进入英语。

items.en: Famine also describes severe shortages of other things.
items.cn: 现代英语中 famine 也形容其他事物的严重短缺。

note.en: Famine is compared with similar spellings and with words for hunger and shortage.
note.cn: 把 famine 与形近词以及表示饥饿和短缺的词作比较。

entries.definition: suffering or death from lack of food

normalIntro.en: Famine sounds like famous minus the last syllable, and famous people never face it.
normalIntro.cn: famine 像去掉末音节的 famous，而名人们不会遭遇饥荒。

normal.en: Famine and famished share the idea of extreme hunger.
normal.cn: famine 与 famished 都含极度饥饿之意。

normal.en: A famine leaves empty granaries and empty plates.
normal.cn: 饥荒留下空粮仓和空盘子。

normal.en: Drought often comes before famine.
normal.cn: 干旱常常先于饥荒出现。

normal.en: Famine relief is aid sent to hungry people.
normal.cn: famine relief 是送往饥饿人群的援助。

normal.en: The plural famines refers to several periods of hunger.
normal.cn: 复数 famines 指多个饥荒时期。

abstract.en: Famine is not only missing food but broken distribution.
abstract.cn: 饥荒不只是缺粮，也是分配失灵。

abstract.en: A rich world can still suffer a famine of care.
abstract.cn: 富足的世界仍可能缺乏关怀。

abstract.en: The word turns an empty field into a human disaster.
abstract.cn: 这个词把空荡的田地变成人间灾难。

examples.en: The country suffered a famine after the harvest failed.
examples.cn: 收成失败后，这个国家遭遇了饥荒。

examples.en: Aid workers brought food to the famine victims.
examples.cn: 救援人员给饥荒灾民送去食物。

examples.en: The report warned of a famine of affordable housing.
examples.cn: 报告警告可负担住房严重匮乏。

dict_mnemonic.text: famine 与 famished（饿极的）同族，核心是「吃不上饭」；一场大范围缺粮就是饥荒。

root: 源自拉丁语 fames（饥饿），经古法语 famine 入英语，核心义「大范围因缺粮而挨饿」。

sensesIntro.en: Famine means widespread starvation, extreme hunger, or a severe shortage of something.
sensesIntro.cn: famine 意为大范围饥荒、极度饥饿，或某物的严重缺乏。

core.en: A large-scale lack of food causing hunger.
core.cn: 造成饥饿的大范围食物短缺。

branches.en: The core disaster of mass starvation.
branches.cn: 大规模饥饿的核心灾难。

branches.en: The felt hunger of people and animals.
branches.cn: 人与动物感受到的饥饿。

branches.en: Severe shortage extended beyond food.
branches.cn: 超出食物范围的严重短缺。

branches.en: Food shortage and felt hunger define a famine.
branches.cn: 缺粮与饥饿感共同构成饥荒。

branches.en: Both are extreme scarcity with serious results.
branches.cn: 两者都是造成严重后果的极度稀缺。

intro.en: Famine has a small family around hunger and relief.
intro.cn: famine 有一个围绕饥饿与救济的小词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin fames, hunger, is the source of the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fames（饥饿）是该词族的来源。

items.exampleCN: 该地区经历了多次饥荒。

items.example: The old text says famish the enemy.

items.exampleCN: 饥荒灾民需要干净的水。
遭受饥荒的地区需要帮助。

items.example: The agency issued a famine warning.

definition_en: the ability to see; the range within which you can see; the ability to judge
core_image: 远处字母表在眼前逐渐清晰或模糊
scene: 随着年龄增长，他的视力变差了。 His eyesight grew worse with age.
sceneCN: 这里 eyesight 是「视力」（第 1 个义项）；句意：随着年龄增长，他的视力变差了。

senses.title: The ability to see
senses.definition: the ability of the eyes to see
senses.definitionCN: 眼睛观看的能力
senses.example: Good eyesight is important for driving.
senses.exampleCN: 好视力对开车很重要。
senses.why: The core sense is the power of the eyes.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是眼睛的观看能力。

senses.title: Range of vision
senses.definition: the distance within which things can be seen
senses.definitionCN: 能够看见事物的距离范围
senses.example: The plane disappeared from eyesight.
senses.exampleCN: 飞机从视野中消失了。
senses.why: The ability becomes the range it covers.
senses.whyCN: 能力变成它所覆盖的范围。

senses.title: Judgment
senses.definition: the ability to judge or notice things well
senses.definitionCN: 善于判断或察觉事物的能力
senses.example: His business eyesight is respected.
senses.exampleCN: 他的商业眼光受人尊敬。
senses.why: Physical sight becomes mental insight.
senses.whyCN: 身体上的视觉变成心智上的洞察。

intro.en: Eyesight joins eye and sight, two Old English words for seeing.
intro.cn: eyesight 由 eye 与 sight 组成，两者都是古英语中与「看」有关的词。

items.en: Eage names the organ of sight.
items.cn: eage 指观看的器官。

items.en: Sihth names the act or power of seeing.
items.cn: sihth 指看的动作或能力。

items.en: The two words join to name the power of the eyes.
items.cn: 两个词组合起来指眼睛的能力。

items.en: Eyesight becomes the common word for vision.
items.cn: 中古英语中 eyesight 成为表示视力的常用词。

items.en: Eyesight also covers range and judgment.
items.cn: 现代英语中 eyesight 也涵盖视野与眼光。

note.en: Eyesight is the power to see; insight is deep understanding.
note.cn: eyesight 是看的能力，insight 则是深刻的理解。

entries.definition: the power or act of seeing
what can be seen from a place

normalIntro.en: Eyesight is the power of the eyes to see clearly.
normalIntro.cn: eyesight 是眼睛清楚观看的能力。

normal.en: His eyesight is poor without glasses.
normal.cn: 不戴眼镜时他的视力很差。

normal.en: The test checks the eyesight of drivers.
normal.cn: 这项测试检查司机的视力。

normal.en: She lost her eyesight in one eye.
normal.cn: 她一只眼睛失明了。

normal.en: Good eyesight helped him spot the bird.
normal.cn: 好视力让他发现了那只鸟。

normal.en: Failing eyesight made reading difficult.
normal.cn: 视力衰退让阅读变得困难。

abstract.en: Picture letters on a chart fading into blur.
abstract.cn: 想象视力表上的字母渐渐变模糊。

abstract.en: Imagine a distant ship slowly leaving view.
abstract.cn: 想象远处的船慢慢离开视野。

abstract.en: Think of a sharp image coming into focus.
abstract.cn: 想象清晰的画面逐渐对焦。

examples.en: Regular tests can protect your eyesight.
examples.cn: 定期检查可以保护视力。

examples.en: His eyesight is still sharp at eighty.
examples.cn: 他八十岁视力仍然敏锐。

examples.en: The bird flew out of eyesight.
examples.cn: 鸟儿飞出了视野。

dict_mnemonic.text: eye（眼睛）加 sight（看），两者合起来就是眼睛看的能力，即 eyesight（视力）。

root: 由 eye 与 sight 复合而成，两者都源自古英语中与「看」有关的词，核心义「眼睛的观看能力」。

sensesIntro.en: Eyesight means the ability to see, the range of vision, or good judgment.
sensesIntro.cn: eyesight 意为观看能力、视野范围，或良好的判断力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: letters coming into focus on a chart.
core.cn: 核心意象：视力表上的字母逐渐清晰。

branches.en: The base sense is the power to see.
branches.cn: 基础义是观看的能力。

branches.en: The ability becomes the range it covers.
branches.cn: 能力变成它所覆盖的范围。

branches.en: Physical sight becomes mental judgment.
branches.cn: 身体视觉变成心智判断。

branches.en: Clear sight and wide range support each other.
branches.cn: 清晰视力与宽广视野相互支持。

branches.en: Seeing well and judging well share the eye.
branches.cn: 看得清与判断准都离不开眼睛。

intro.en: Eyesight is a compound of two native English words about seeing.
intro.cn: eyesight 由两个表示「看」的英语本族词复合而成。

latinIntro.en: Eyesight has no Latin root; both parts are Old English.
latinIntro.cn: eyesight 没有拉丁词根，两个部分都来自古英语。

items.example: Sight is one of the five senses.
The center helps sighted and blind people.
items.exampleCN: 这个中心帮助视力正常者与盲人。

items.example: He is short-sighted in one eye.

items.meaning: unable to see near things clearly
items.example: She is long-sighted and needs glasses.

items.exampleCN: 头脑清醒的领导者会提前规划。

items.example: The book gives insight into history.
items.exampleCN: 这本书让人深入了解历史。

definition_en: to become healthy again, to make a wound or illness go away, or to repair a relationship
core_image: 伤口慢慢收口，最后只留下一道浅痕
scene: 小伤口几天后就愈合了。 The small cut healed in a few days.
sceneCN: 这里 heal 是「痊愈」（第 1 个义项）；句意：小伤口几天后就愈合了。

senses.title: Become well again
senses.definition: to become healthy again after an injury or illness
senses.definitionCN: 受伤或生病之后重新恢复健康
senses.example: The small cut healed in a few days.
senses.exampleCN: 小伤口几天后就愈合了。
senses.why: This is the body repairing itself.
senses.whyCN: 这是身体自我修复的过程。

senses.title: Make someone well
senses.definition: to make a wound or a sick person healthy again
senses.definitionCN: 使伤口愈合或使病人恢复健康
senses.example: Time can heal a broken bone.
senses.exampleCN: 时间能让断骨长好。
senses.why: The subject here does the curing, not the receiving.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项里主语是施治者，而不是被治愈的人。

senses.title: Repair a bond
senses.definition: to repair a relationship or end a disagreement
senses.definitionCN: 修复关系或结束分歧
senses.example: The two brothers finally healed the rift.
senses.exampleCN: 两兄弟终于弥合了裂痕。
senses.why: A broken trust is treated like a broken body.
senses.whyCN: 破裂的信任被当成了受伤的身体。

intro.en: Heal comes from Old English hælan, to make whole.
intro.cn: heal 来自古英语 hælan，意为使完整。

items.en: Hælan meant to make whole or sound.
items.cn: hælan 意为使完整、使健全。

items.en: The same root named health and wholeness.
items.cn: 同一词根也构成了 health 与完整之意。

items.en: Helen kept the sense of curing the body.
items.cn: 中古英语拼作 helen，仍指医治身体。

items.en: Heal also described wounds closing by themselves.
items.cn: heal 也开始指伤口自行收口。

items.en: The word stretched to mending feelings and ties.
items.cn: 这个词又扩展到修补情感与关系。

note.en: Heal is compared with look-alike words and with words for getting better.
note.cn: 把 heal 与形近词以及表示好转的词作比较。

entries.definition: the back part of the foot
to make an illness go away

normalIntro.en: Heal is the quiet work of becoming whole again.
normalIntro.cn: heal 是重新变得完整的安静过程。

normal.en: The wound healed quickly.
normal.cn: 伤口很快愈合了。

normal.en: She helped heal the old quarrel.
normal.cn: 她帮忙弥合了那场旧争吵。

normal.en: Rest helps the body heal.
normal.cn: 休息有助于身体康复。

normal.en: The doctor healed many patients.
normal.cn: 这位医生治愈了许多病人。

normal.en: Time heals most hurts.
normal.cn: 时间能抚平大多数伤痛。

abstract.en: Healing is wholeness returning.
abstract.cn: 愈合，就是完整重新回来。

abstract.en: A scar is proof that repair happened.
abstract.cn: 疤痕是修复发生过的证据。

abstract.en: Broken trust heals more slowly than bone.
abstract.cn: 破裂的信任，比骨头好得更慢。

examples.en: The small cut healed in a few days.
examples.cn: 小伤口几天后就愈合了。

examples.en: The two brothers finally healed the rift.
examples.cn: 两兄弟终于弥合了裂痕。

examples.en: Sun and rest helped heal his leg.
examples.cn: 阳光和休息帮助他的腿痊愈。

dict_mnemonic.text: heal 与 health 同源，本义是「使完整」；伤口长好是痊愈，医生治好是治愈，关系修补好是弥合。

root: 来自古英语 hælan（使完整、使健全），与 health、whole 同源；由身体的完整，引申为伤病的痊愈，再扩展到关系与情感的修复。

sensesIntro.en: Heal moves from a body closing its wound to a doctor curing, and then to mending a bond.
sensesIntro.cn: heal 从身体收口，走到医生施治，再走到关系的修补。

core.en: A cut slowly closing over.
core.cn: 一道伤口慢慢合上。

branches.en: The skin joins again by itself.
branches.cn: 皮肤自己重新连在一起。

branches.en: A doctor treats the sick.
branches.cn: 医生医治病人。

branches.en: Two old friends speak again.
branches.cn: 两位老朋友重新开口说话。

branches.en: The body and the healer work together.
branches.cn: 身体与医者一起用力。

branches.en: What cures a wound can also cure a quarrel.
branches.cn: 能治好伤口的，也能治好争吵。

intro.en: Heal takes verb endings and builds agent, action, and negative forms.
intro.cn: heal 加动词词尾，并构成施动者、动作与否定形式。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

definition_zh: 体贴的；为他人着想的；考虑周到的
definition_en: careful not to upset others, and thoughtful about their needs
core_image: 深夜回宿舍的人握住钥匙，慢慢转动门锁
scene: 夜归的人把钥匙握在手心，轻轻转动门锁。 It was considerate of her to call first.
sceneCN: 这里 considerate 指「体贴的」（第 1 个义项：顾及他人感受）；句意是她先打了个电话，真是体贴。

pos.zh: 体贴的；为他人着想的；考虑周到的

senses.title: Thinking of others
senses.definition: careful about other people's feelings and needs
senses.definitionCN: 在意他人的感受与需要
senses.example: It was considerate of her to call first.
senses.exampleCN: 她先打了个电话，真体贴。
senses.why: A small act says that another person is real to you.
senses.whyCN: 一个小动作，说明另一个人在你心里是真实的。

senses.title: Thoughtful in action
senses.definition: showing care in what one does or says
senses.definitionCN: 在言行中表现出用心
senses.example: He left a considerate note on the table.
senses.exampleCN: 他在桌上留了一张体贴的便条。
senses.why: Care becomes visible only when it moves a hand or a word.
senses.whyCN: 用心只有推动了一只手或一句话，才变得可见。

senses.title: Careful by design
senses.definition: showing careful thought rather than haste, an older sense
senses.definitionCN: 表现出仔细思量而非匆忙，是较古老的义项
senses.example: His considerate reply avoided every sharp word.
senses.exampleCN: 他那番经过思量的回答避开了所有锋利的词。
senses.why: The word once meant thought-through before it meant kind.
senses.whyCN: 这个词在表示善良之前，先表示想清楚了。

intro.en: Considerate comes from Latin consideratus, examined and thought over, from considerare, to look at closely.
intro.cn: considerate 来自拉丁语 consideratus，意为经过审视与思量的，源头是 considerare（仔细看）。

items.en: Considerare meant to examine something with care.
items.cn: considerare 意为用心审视某物。

items.en: Consideratus described a matter already weighed in the mind.
items.cn: consideratus 描述的是心里已经掂量过的事。

items.en: English considerate first meant deliberate and thoughtful.
items.cn: 英语 considerate 最初指深思熟虑的。

items.en: It shifted toward thought for other people's comfort.
items.cn: 它的含义转向对他人舒适感受的照顾。

items.en: Today it names the habit of not troubling others.
items.cn: 如今它指不给人添麻烦的习惯。

note.en: The look-alike group is the consider family, and the meaning group names other words for caring about others.
note.cn: 形近组是 consider 家族，近义组列出其他表示关心他人的词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a key turned slowly, then move to a note left on a table and to a reply with no sharp edges.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从慢慢转动的钥匙开始，再到留在桌上的便条，最后到一句没有棱角的回答。

normal.en: Considerate is consider plus -ate: someone who thinks about you before acting.
normal.cn: considerate 是 consider 加 -ate：行动之前先想到你的人。

normal.en: A considerate person closes doors as if someone is asleep.
normal.cn: 体贴的人关门时，像屋里有人正在睡觉。

normal.en: Leaving the last seat for someone else is the whole idea.
normal.cn: 把最后一个座位留给别人，就是这个词的全部意思。

normal.en: It is not politeness of form, but attention of mind.
normal.cn: 它不是形式上的礼貌，而是心思上的在意。

normal.en: If your act costs you little and saves another much, it is considerate.
normal.cn: 若你的举动花费很小、却让别人省下很多，那就是体贴。

abstract.en: Picture a door easing shut without a sound.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门无声地慢慢合上。

abstract.en: Picture a cup of water set beside a sleeping friend.
abstract.cn: 想象一杯水放在熟睡的朋友身边。

abstract.en: Picture a chair pulled out for someone older.
abstract.cn: 想象为年长者拉开的一把椅子。

examples.en: It was considerate of her to call first.
examples.cn: 她先打了电话，真体贴。

examples.en: He is always considerate towards new students.
examples.cn: 他对新来的学生总是很体贴。

examples.en: A considerate reply can end an argument.
examples.cn: 一句体贴的回答可以结束一场争吵。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 considerate 记成 consider（考虑）加 ate：做事之前先考虑到别人，就是体贴。

root: 源自拉丁语 consideratus（经过审视的），由 considerare 加 -ate 构成，本义是想得周到，后专指体贴他人。

sensesIntro.en: From careful thought, to thought turned toward other people, and finally to the small acts that prove it.
sensesIntro.cn: 从仔细思量，到把思量转向别人，最后到证明这一点的小动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key turned slowly so no one wakes.
core.cn: 核心意象：钥匙慢慢转动，好不吵醒任何人。

branches.en: The first sense is care for another person's feelings.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是在意另一个人的感受。

branches.en: The second sense makes that care visible in words or acts.
branches.cn: 第二个义项让这份在意在言行中显露出来。

branches.en: The older sense stresses thought before action.
branches.cn: 较古老的义项强调行动之前的思量。

branches.en: Feeling for others and acting on it belong together.
branches.cn: 替别人感受与照着去做，本来就是一回事。

branches.en: A careful act is both thought through and kind.
branches.cn: 周到的举动，既经过思量，也带着善意。

intro.en: Considerate is consider plus -ate, from Latin consideratus, thought over.
intro.cn: considerate 是 consider 加 -ate，源自拉丁语 consideratus（经过思量的）。

latinIntro.en: The star base sider- also appears in sidereal, and the same root shaped desire.
latinIntro.cn: 星辰词基 sider- 也出现在 sidereal 中，同一个词根也塑造了 desire。

items.exampleCN: 体贴的主人会先问一声。
这么大声放音乐很不体谅人。
对安静的渴望越来越强。

definition_en: enjoyable activity that refreshes the mind or body; the restoring of health; the act of creating again
core_image: 公园长椅上的人放下工作，笑着望向湖面
scene: 周末的公园里，有人骑车，有人铺开野餐布。 Gardening is his favourite form of recreation.
sceneCN: 这里 recreation 是「消遣」（第 1 个义项：让人放松的娱乐活动）；句意为园艺是他最喜欢的消遣。画面里可留意：骑车的人、铺开的野餐布。

senses.title: Enjoyable activity
senses.definition: an activity done for enjoyment that refreshes the mind or body
senses.definitionCN: 为获得乐趣、使身心恢复而做的事
senses.example: Gardening is his favourite form of recreation.
senses.exampleCN: 园艺是他最喜欢的消遣。
senses.why: Recreare meant to restore, and the noun first named the restoring of health before it named the games that do the restoring.
senses.whyCN: recreare 意为恢复，这个名词先指恢复健康，后来才指带来恢复的娱乐活动。

senses.title: The restoring of strength
senses.definition: the act of recovering strength and health after work or illness
senses.definitionCN: 在工作或生病之后恢复体力与健康的行为
senses.example: He walked by the sea for recreation after the illness.
senses.exampleCN: 病后他在海边散步休养。
senses.why: The older sense is recovery, and a walk taken to restore the body keeps that meaning alive.
senses.whyCN: 较早的意思是恢复，而为了调养身体所走的散步，正是这层含义的延续。

senses.title: The act of creating again
senses.definition: the act of making something again or of reproducing a scene or an event
senses.definitionCN: 重新制作某物，或再现某个场景与事件
senses.example: The film is a recreation of the battle rather than a record.
senses.exampleCN: 这部影片是对那场战役的再现，而不是记录。
senses.why: When re- is read as again and create as to make, the word can literally mean a second making.
senses.whyCN: 当 re- 被读作「再次」、create 被读作「制作」时，这个词就可以字面地表示「第二次制作」。

intro.en: Recreation begins as restoration: the body is made fresh again, and the activities that do this take the name.
intro.cn: recreation 始于「恢复」：身体被重新造得清新，而带来这种效果的活动便沿用了这个名字。

items.en: Creare meant to create, produce, or bring forth, the root of the family.
items.cn: creare 意为创造、产生或带来，是整个词族的词根。

items.en: Recreare joined re-, again, to creare and meant to restore or refresh.
items.cn: recreare 由 re-（再次）与 creare 组成，意为恢复或使清新。

items.en: Old French recreacion carried the noun into English as refreshment.
items.cn: 古法语 recreacion 把这个名词带入英语，意为恢复精神。

items.en: English first used recreation for the restoring of health after labour.
items.cn: 英语最初用 recreation 指劳作之后的恢复。

items.en: Modern English widened the word to the games and hobbies that refresh people.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个词扩展到使人恢复的游戏与爱好。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns from the same create family; the near-meaning group gathers words for leisure and amusement.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 create 词族的名词；近义组收表休闲与娱乐的词。

entries.definition: The act of making something new.
The act of making something again.
A hobby that passes the time pleasantly.

normalIntro.en: The word is creating again: energy that was used up is made fresh, and the activity that does it is called recreation.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「重新创造」：耗掉的精力被重新造出，而做这件事的活动就叫 recreation。

normal.en: Re plus creation: a second making, this time of your own strength.
normal.cn: re 加 creation：第二次创造，这次造的是你自己的精力。

normal.en: Outdoor recreation means games played in the open air.
normal.cn: outdoor recreation 指在户外进行的活动。

normal.en: A recreation centre is a building for leisure activities.
normal.cn: recreation centre 是供休闲活动的场所。

normal.en: Recreation and re-creation differ by a hyphen and by their meaning.
normal.cn: recreation 与 re-creation 只差一个连字符，意思却不同。

normal.en: The noun is uncountable when it means leisure, countable when it means a re-enactment.
normal.cn: 表休闲时不可数，表「再现」时可数。

abstract.en: Recreation is the art of making the self fresh again.
abstract.cn: 消遣是让自我重新清新的艺术。

abstract.en: What restores a person is not idleness but a different kind of effort.
abstract.cn: 让人恢复的不是闲散，而是另一种努力。

abstract.en: A society shows its values in what it chooses to do for recreation.
abstract.cn: 一个社会选择以什么为消遣，就显露出它的价值。

examples.en: Gardening is his favourite form of recreation.
examples.cn: 园艺是他最喜欢的消遣。

examples.en: He walked by the sea for recreation after the illness.
examples.cn: 病后他在海边散步休养。

examples.en: The film is a recreation of the battle rather than a record.
examples.cn: 这部影片是对那场战役的再现，而不是记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（重新）加 create（创造）：把耗掉的精力重新造回来，就是休养；用来休养的活动，就是消遣。

root: 拉丁 creare（创造）→ recreare（恢复、重新振作）→ 古法语 recreacion → 英语 recreation；同族有 recreational、recreate。

sensesIntro.en: The core is restoration; the senses move from restoring health to the activities that restore it and to a second making of a scene.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「恢复」；义项从恢复健康，到带来恢复的活动，再到对场景的再次制作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a park bench where someone sets down their work and smiles at the lake.
core.cn: 核心意象：公园长椅上的人放下工作，笑着望向湖面。

branches.en: a picnic blanket on grass
branches.cn: 草地上铺开的野餐布

branches.en: a slow walk by the sea
branches.cn: 海边缓慢的散步

branches.en: a film set rebuilding a battle
branches.cn: 重建战役场景的片场

branches.en: a game and the strength it restores
branches.cn: 游戏与它恢复的精力

branches.en: a body remade and a scene remade
branches.cn: 身体被重建，场景也被重建

intro.en: A Latin verb of creating takes a prefix of repetition and a noun ending, and the result names both rest and re-enactment.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的「创造」动词接上表重复的前缀与名词词尾，结果既指休息，也指再现。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is creare, to create, changed by re- and named by -tio.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 creare（创造），由 re- 加以改变，并由 -tio 名词化。

definition_zh: 不寻常地；特别地；异常地；非常
definition_en: more than is usual, or in a way that is not common
core_image: 整条街都安静，只有一扇窗还亮着灯
scene: 三月里竟下起了雪，院子里那株桃树的花全被压低了。 It snowed unusually late this year.
sceneCN: 这里 unusually 是「异常地、不寻常地」（第 1 个义项：超出常态）；句意为今年下雪下得反常地晚。整条街只有一扇窗亮着，正是这个词的核心画面。

pos.zh: 非常；特别（放在形容词前）

derivatives.zh: 副词去掉 -ly 的形容词形式，义为「不寻常的」
去掉否定前缀的形容词，义为「通常的」
肯定形式加 -ly 的副词，义为「通常」
形容词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不寻常」

senses.title: More than normal in degree
senses.definition: used before an adjective to say the degree is greater than usual
senses.definitionCN: 放在形容词前，说明程度超出平常
senses.example: The winter was unusually mild this year.
senses.exampleCN: 今年的冬天反常地温和。
senses.why: The prefix negates usual, and before an adjective the word simply marks a degree that departs from the norm.
senses.whyCN: 前缀否定了 usual（通常的），放在形容词前时，这个词只标记一种偏离常态的程度。

senses.title: In a way that is not common
senses.definition: used of behaviour or events that rarely happen
senses.definitionCN: 形容罕见的行为或事件
senses.example: She was unusually silent during dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 晚饭时她异常沉默。
senses.why: What departs from the usual way also departs from the usual amount.
senses.whyCN: 偏离寻常方式的东西，也偏离了寻常的分量。

senses.title: Attached to weather and numbers
senses.definition: used with measurements to signal a figure outside the usual range
senses.definitionCN: 与测量数值连用，表示数字超出通常范围
senses.example: Prices rose unusually fast in the first quarter.
senses.exampleCN: 第一季度物价上涨得反常地快。
senses.why: Figures are compared with past figures, so a number off the pattern is called unusual.
senses.whyCN: 数字要和以往比，脱离规律的数字就被称为不寻常。

senses.title: As an intensifier close to very
senses.definition: used informally to mean remarkably or very
senses.definitionCN: 口语中可理解为「非常、格外」
senses.example: He is an unusually patient teacher.
senses.exampleCN: 他是位格外有耐心的老师。
senses.why: Great rarity in degree feels like great strength, so the word drifts towards very.
senses.whyCN: 程度上的罕见感会觉得像强度，于是这个词向 very 靠拢。
